sourceNote: Sohra is the Khasi name; Cherrapunji and Cherrapunjee are widely used aliases. At ~1484m on the Khasi Hills escarpment, formerly the wettest place on earth. Best season Oct–Apr (waterfalls flow year-round but Jul–Sep monsoon has cloud cover and slippery paths). All records curated from Wikipedia and documented sources. dataStatus needs_review.

places.name: Nohkalikai Falls
places.description: India's tallest plunge waterfall at 340m, dropping from the Khasi plateau escarpment into a turquoise pool below. Named after Ka Likai, a woman from local legend. Viewable from a government-maintained platform at the plateau edge. Most dramatic during monsoon (Jul–Sep); flows year-round, and the plunge pool is strikingly blue-green in post-monsoon months. Entry fee applies; viewpoint is ~200m walk from parking. One of the signature sights of Meghalaya.
places.area: Sohra plateau edge, 6km from Sohra town

places.name: Living Root Bridge, Nongriat
places.description: Double-decker living root bridge formed over 500 years by training the aerial roots of Indian rubber trees (Ficus elastica) across a stream in Nongriat village. The famous double-decker bridge is one of the most photographed natural structures in India. Access involves a steep descent of ~3500 steps from the Tyrna trailhead (9km from Sohra), 90–120 minutes each way. Village stay possible at Nongriat. A strenuous but uniquely rewarding hike. The Wahthyllong and other single-tier root bridges in surrounding villages are less visited.
places.openingDays: Open all day; hike in daylight only

places.name: Mawsmai Cave
places.description: Illuminated limestone cave 6km from Sohra, formed by the Mawsmai stream over millennia. The 150-metre tourist circuit passes through formations of stalactites, stalagmites, and narrow passageways. One of the most accessible caves in Meghalaya — lit throughout and walkable without specialist equipment. Entry fee applies. Gets busy in peak season; early morning visits are quieter. Surrounding area has a few other caves (Kutmadan, Liat Prah) that require local guides.

places.name: Eco Park Sohra
places.description: Government-run park on the escarpment of Sohra with viewpoints overlooking the Khasi Hills gorges and, on clear days, the plains of Bangladesh. The park serves primarily as a vantage point for the dramatic landscape. Several viewpoints within the park offer different angles; interpretation boards describe the ecology of the plateau. Modest entry fee. Often misty in the morning; afternoon light on clear Oct–Mar days is excellent.

places.name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
places.description: Seven-segmented waterfall on the Khasi escarpment, dropping approximately 315m to the valley below. During monsoon (Jun–Sep) all seven streams run together in a dramatic wall of water; in the drier months the flow is thinner but the rock face is still impressive. Often photographed against the Bangladesh plains in the distance. Viewable from the road near Sohra and from Eco Park. One of the most spectacular escarpment waterfalls in Northeast India; also known as the Seven Sisters Falls.
places.area: Sohra escarpment, 5km south of Sohra town

places.name: Thangkharang Park
places.description: Hillside park on the southern escarpment of Sohra, 12km from town, with viewpoints overlooking the plains of Bangladesh. On extremely clear October–November mornings, the Sylhet plains are visible stretching to the horizon. The park has a small botanical garden, a pathway to a lower viewpoint, and the Ka Kshaid Duli Syntu spring. A Jaintia-era cannon is on display. Entry fee. The Kynrem Falls (3-tier, 305m) is visible from within the park grounds.

places.name: Arwah Cave
places.description: Limestone cave near Mawmluh village, 7km from Sohra, notable for fossil invertebrate specimens embedded in the cave walls — visible without specialist lighting. The main chamber is broad with high ceilings; a river flows through sections, making rubber boots advisable. The fossils represent marine organisms from an ancient seabed (the Khasi Hills were once beneath the Tethys Sea). Less commercialised than Mawsmai; guided visits recommended. Longer and more exploratory than Mawsmai Cave.

places.name: Dainthlen Falls
places.description: Broad waterfall near Sohra town, framed in Khasi legend as the site where the serpent Thlen was killed by a hero using a sword. The falls drop over a wide rock step into a pool; accessible by a short path from the road. Less dramatic than Nohkalikai but more accessible and often quieter. The surrounding rocks are layered sandstone; geology enthusiasts will appreciate the visible strata. No formal entry fee at most times.

places.name: Wei Sawdong Falls
places.description: Three-tier waterfall in the valley below Tyrna village, a 40-minute hike from the start of the Nongriat root-bridge trail. Quieter and less visited than the Double-Decker Root Bridge, Wei Sawdong offers swimming in clear pools at the base of each tier. A worthwhile detour when combining with the Nongriat hike. Rocky path; appropriate footwear essential. The pools are cool and clean.
places.openingDays: Open all day; hike in daylight only

places.name: Mawkdok Dympep Valley Viewpoint
places.description: Valley viewpoint on the Shillong–Sohra highway, 15km north of Sohra, where the road reaches the plateau edge and drops sharply into the Mawkdok gorge. The sudden view of the deep, forested canyon is one of the most striking sights on the Shillong–Sohra road. A commercial operator runs a zip-line (flying fox) across part of the valley. The roadside stop is free; the zip-line activity is charged separately. Often included as a stop when driving from Shillong to Sohra.
places.area: Mawkdok, on Shillong–Sohra highway, 15km from Sohra
